scenario: Asthma follow-up in a man whose control has worsened after stopping his steroid inhaler; combiflam makes him wheeze.

turns.speaker: Doctor
turns.text: Hello Vikram, good to see you again. How has the month been?

turns.speaker: Patient
turns.text: Not so good, doctor. The weather has turned humid and the chest has been tight again. I have come for my asthma check, and it is worse.

turns.speaker: Doctor
turns.text: How often are you getting symptoms?

turns.speaker: Patient
turns.text: Daytime, two or three times a week. And at night I wake up coughing, maybe two nights a week, um, sometimes three.

turns.speaker: Doctor
turns.text: And since when has it been worse?

turns.speaker: Patient
turns.text: For the last month, since the humid weather started. Before that it was fine for almost six months.

turns.speaker: Doctor
turns.text: Any fever, chest pain, or yellow phlegm?

turns.speaker: Patient
turns.text: No fever, no chest pain, no phlegm. Just dry cough and wheezing, mostly after exercise. I played cricket on Sunday and had to stop after ten minutes.

turns.speaker: Doctor
turns.text: What inhalers are you using at the moment?

turns.speaker: Patient
turns.text: The blue one, asthalin, I use it about five times a week now. Before it was once a week. And I stopped the other inhaler, the brown one, in February because I felt fine.

turns.speaker: Doctor
turns.text: Do you remember the name on the brown inhaler box?

turns.speaker: Patient
turns.text: Um, foracort, I think. Yes, foracort.

turns.speaker: Doctor
turns.text: Any allergies to medicines, or anything that triggers your asthma?

turns.speaker: Patient
turns.text: Combiflam makes me wheeze, so I stay away from it. Dust and cold air also trigger it.

turns.speaker: Doctor
turns.text: Good that you avoid it. Any past illness, and any family history?

turns.speaker: Patient
turns.text: Asthma since I was a child. I had pneumonia once, last winter. My mother also has asthma.

turns.speaker: Doctor
turns.text: Let me examine you. Your pulse is 84 and oxygen is 97. I can hear some wheeze at the end of breathing out, on both sides.

turns.speaker: Patient
turns.text: Is that bad?

turns.speaker: Doctor
turns.text: Your peak flow is 420, which is lower than your usual. I think your asthma is not well controlled at the moment, mostly because you stopped the steroid inhaler.

turns.speaker: Patient
turns.text: Doctor, will I be able to play cricket again? And is this going to get worse every monsoon?

turns.speaker: Doctor
turns.text: Yes, you can play once it is under control. Use two puffs of the blue inhaler ten minutes before. Let me restart the foracort, two puffs twice a day, and add montelukast 10 milligrams at night. Rinse your mouth after each puff.

turns.speaker: Patient
turns.text: Should I do any test?

turns.speaker: Doctor
turns.text: Yes, a lung function test, spirometry, once you are settled. We can book it for next time.

turns.speaker: Patient
turns.text: Okay.

turns.speaker: Doctor
turns.text: Review in six weeks. If you need the blue inhaler more than every day, or you cannot speak a full sentence, come immediately.

turns.speaker: Patient
turns.text: Thank you, doctor. See you.

gold.key: asthma since i was a child
some wheeze at the end of breathing out
will i be able to play cricket again
use two puffs of the blue inhaler ten minutes before
rinse your mouth after each puff

notes: Weather remarks are mixed into the clinical statements in turn 1 and not labelled separately. Cricket appears both as a symptom trigger in turn 7 (unlabelled) and as a genuine patient concern in turn 19. Frequency statements (two or three times a week) are not durations and are unlabelled. Turn 9: the brown inhaler is not named by the patient until turn 11 (hedged then confirmed, labelled certain). Turn 13 is a drug reaction (combiflam makes me wheeze) and also lists non-drug triggers, which are unlabelled. Peak flow is a measurement stated by the doctor and is labelled vital_sign. The patient takes asthalin and (until February) foracort; the doctor restarts foracort and adds montelukast. Turn 24 return-immediately advice is hypothetical and is not a red_flag.
